betokening.meaning: Showing clearly that something is true; being a sign of it.

conservatory.meaning: A glass room, kept warm, where plants grow all year. It is part of a rich house.

listless.meaning: Tired and without interest or energy.

sallied.meaning: Went out quickly and bravely to do something.

pate.meaning: The head, or the top of the head. Here it is a funny word for Laurie's hair-covered head.

blancmange.meaning: A soft, sweet, white food made from milk. It is cold and smooth and is eaten with a spoon.

fidgety.meaning: Not able to keep still; always moving and worried.

elated.meaning: Very happy and proud because something good has happened.

redoubtable.meaning: Strong, and a little hard to face; a person you must respect.

evolutions.meaning: Planned movements. Here the boy makes funny movements to make a girl laugh.

glowered.meaning: Looked at someone with an angry, dark face.

gruff.meaning: Rough and low in voice or manner, but not truly unkind.

quaint.meaning: Old-fashioned in a pleasing, interesting way.

woo.meaning: To try to win the love of a person so that she will say yes to marriage.

paragraphs.context: Meg went back to toast her feet and read Ivanhoe
paragraphs.mainIdea: Jo digs paths in the snow. The garden is between the Marches' shabby old house and the rich, lonely Laurence house.
paragraphs.simple: Meg went back to warm her feet and read Ivanhoe, and Jo began to dig paths with great energy. The snow was light, and with her broom she soon swept a path all round the garden, for Beth to walk in when the sun came out. The sick dolls needed air. The garden was between the Marches' house and Mr. Laurence's house. Both stood at the edge of the city, which still looked like the country, with small woods, lawns, large gardens and quiet streets. A low hedge divided the two properties. On one side was an old brown house that looked rather bare and shabby, because the vines that covered its walls in summer, and the flowers around it, were gone. On the other side was a fine stone house that clearly showed every kind of comfort and wealth, from the big coach-house and well-kept grounds to the greenhouse and the lovely things people could see between the rich curtains. But it seemed a lonely house with no life in it. No children played on the lawn, no mother's face smiled at the windows, and few people went in or out, except the old gentleman and his grandson.

paragraphs.context: I am not sure, but I think it was because his son
paragraphs.mainIdea: Mrs. March thinks she knows why Mr. Laurence dislikes Laurie's music. It reminds him of Laurie's Italian mother, whom he did not like.
paragraphs.simple: I am not sure, but I think it was because his son, Laurie's father, married an Italian lady who was a musician. This made the proud old man angry. The lady was good, lovely and skilled, but he did not like her, and he never saw his son again after the marriage. Both of them died when Laurie was a small child, and then his grandfather took him home. I think the boy, who was born in Italy, is not very strong, and the old man is afraid of losing him, so he is very careful. Laurie gets his love of music naturally, because he is like his mother. I dare say his grandfather fears that he may want to be a musician. In any case, Laurie's skill reminds the old man of the woman he did not like, and so he 'glowered', as Jo said.

sentences.context: The atmosphere of the whole house being summer-like, Laurie led the way
sentences.simple: Because the whole house felt warm like summer, Laurie led the way from room to room.
sentences.grammar: 'The atmosphere ... being summer-like' is an absolute phrase with its own subject. It gives the reason for what follows.

sentences.context: Shouldn't ask you, if I didn't
sentences.simple: I would not ask you if I did not want you to come.
sentences.grammar: Short spoken English: the subject 'I' is dropped, and 'want you to' is left out after 'didn't'. It is a short 'if' sentence.

tell on.meaning: To go on telling a story; to keep talking.

put on airs.meaning: To act as if you are better than other people.
put on airs.example: and didn't put on any airs

make much of.meaning: To show that you like a person very much and give him lots of attention.
make much of.example: and made much of him, and he found something

get on.meaning: To be friendly with someone and live or work well with them.
get on.example: she would not have got on at all
